_comment: Generated by `node scripts/check-mcp-delivery.mjs --write-tool-baseline` (task 1559). What each allowlisted local stdio MCP server answered to tools/list: sha256 is over the canonical (sorted-key) JSON of {name, description, inputSchema}. `unverifiable` names why a server was not asked. Regenerate, never hand-edit.

brightdata-web.unverifiable: needs secrets (BRIGHTDATA_API_KEY); a tracked baseline is not taken with operator keys

tools.name: codegraph_explore
tools.description: PRIMARY TOOL — call FIRST for almost any question OR before an edit: how does X work, architecture, a bug, where/what is X, surveying an area, or the symbols you are about to change. Returns the verbatim source of the relevant symbols grouped by file in ONE capped call (Read-equivalent — treat the shown source as already Read; do NOT re-open those files), plus the call path among them. Query can be a natural-language question OR a bag of symbol/file names. Usually the ONLY call you need — more accurate context, in far fewer tokens and round-trips than a search/Read/Grep loop.

query.description: Symbol names, file names, or short code terms to explore (e.g., "AuthService loginUser session-manager", "GraphTraverser BFS impact traversal.ts"). For a flow question, name the symbols spanning the flow (e.g. "mutateElement renderScene"). A natural-language question works too — no prior codegraph_search needed.

maxFiles.description: Maximum number of files to include source code from (default: 12)

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the project to query (or any directory inside it) — codegraph uses the nearest .codegraph/ index at or above that path. Omit to use this session's default project. Pass it to query a second codebase, or when the server root has no index of its own (e.g. a monorepo where only sub-projects are indexed, so there is no default project).

tools.name: memory
tools.description:
Durable project memory (memoryctl). One tool, pick an action.
Reading is three steps and they are not interchangeable: hot says what matters now, search finds WHERE something is written (it answers with a snippet, never the text), get reads that entry whole.
• hot {} — an on-demand digest of what matters now (not injected at session start)
• lessons {path} — durable lessons for a REPO-RELATIVE file; run before editing it
• search {query, kind?, limit?} — search before writing anything; ask in English, and quote a stored title or an exact identifier verbatim to reach a record written in another language. Answers a BARE ARRAY of {id, title, snippet}
• get {id|uuid, follow?} — one entry whole, body included. An id written down earlier names the version live back then: follow:"latest" reads the current one instead, follow:"full_history" adds the lineage root to leaf
• append {kind, title, body, links?, overturns?, closes?} — a durable fact; overturns: ids of live rules it replaces; closes: task ids a DECISION withdraws (closed cancelled, the decision is the evidence; any other kind is refused) (kind: feedback|reference|project|decision), or report to DELIVER a Svod report (body must be the JSON object itself). A report answer naming an id IS the delivery — do NOT re-deliver via the CLI; with no MEMORYCTL_SESSION_ID this route refuses reports and names the CLI command that carries your attempt identity
• supersede {id, title, body, long?} — replace a live entry; lesson replacements pass the brevity gate
• handoff {title, body, tasks?[], no_open_work?, closes?[]} — end of a work chunk. REFUSED unless it declares this session's open tails: tasks:[id,...] or no_open_work:true
• task_create {title, priority, next?, again?, domain?} — priority P0|P1; domain is a routing id (domain-<name>) or null to clear it; a reproduced defect or work the operator agreed to becomes a task, a finished one is closed instead; a title that repeats an existing task is REFUSED by number unless again:true
• task_list {status?} — open tails
• task_done {id, evidence} — close what you finished; evidence (sha | memory#id | what proves it) is REQUIRED
A refusal names every problem at once and ends with the required shape: fix them together, do not re-send to discover the next one. Lessons are NOT written here — use scripts/memory/capture-lesson.mjs so they land in curator quarantine.

args.description: Arguments for the action, as listed in the tool description. Omit for hot.

tools.name: chat_join
tools.description: Bind your lead-chat handle to a session, superseding its previous live binding; optional desktop is get_session "self" field sessionId (at most 80 characters, no whitespace), and rejoining updates only desktop. Use the session id SessionStart prints; no acknowledgement post is wanted.

tools.name: chat_post
tools.description: Post under your live handle to named handles or all, or omit to for a log line; refuses any never-bound named handle and lists live handles, while known handles with no live binding are accepted and returned in `notLive` only when non-empty; a post reaches its addressee at that lead's next own turn, and only `wake` wakes an idle lead: set it when the addressee must act now and the sender cannot continue without that act; pass `class: 'fyi'` to mark a post that must not wake an idle lead, even in reply to a wake post; your first post back to a lead whose wake post reached you in the last 24 h counts as a wake and names that post in `replyWake`; a wake reply lists live addressees with state (watcher, in turn, no watcher), lastSeen and desktop. Use the session id SessionStart prints; no acknowledgement post is wanted.

tools.name: chat_read
tools.description: Read and confirm unread posts for your live handle, or pass all for a read-only log (limit defaults to 50, maximum 200). Use the session id SessionStart prints; no acknowledgement post is wanted.

tools.name: handoff_draft
tools.description: Read-only markdown draft for memoryctl handoff from stored seats and report fields. since: ISO UTC time or turn id (default earliest open seat, else last 12 hours); repo: optional checkout path. Edit before saving to memory.

tools.name: memory_apply
tools.description: Apply a completed turn's stored proposals via memoryctl, sequentially; stops at the first refusal. Inspect the digest first. pick is distinct zero-based indexes; omitted means all. If any picked item is supersede/retire, omitting confirm:true returns a read-only preview of every picked proposal and each live entry's kind/title (memoryctl get). Call again with confirm:true to write. Applied items are not repeated; uncertain writes are never retried automatically.

confirm.description: Required to write when the selection contains supersede or retire.

tools.name: orch_status
tools.description: orch daemon status: version, pid, uptime, schema version, state dir, port, seat counts by status, each family's subscription load (least loaded first, with the reading's age), and each registered host's runtime checkout against the daemon's commit (a host with error is refused or unreachable: its tracked changes are never discarded). Check it before choosing a family.

tools.name: review_plan
tools.description: Suggest reviewer count and concern-based focus over accumulated staged, unstaged and untracked changes (decision #17931). Identical rules for a coder seat, repo with base, or snapshot:true (HEAD vs current tree). Exclude a changed file only when a parent VENDOR.json files entry for its folder-relative path has the SHA-256 of its reviewed Git blob; differing bytes count as own. No upstream network check. VENDOR.json and NOTICE are documentation. Documentation-only stays zero. Jev rates the remaining complete own diff: below 0.2 gives zero, 0.2 to below 0.7 gives one, 0.7 or more gives two. A security path retains at least one; two requires changed own security lines and Jev risk at least 0.7. Security stems: auth, token, secret, credential, security, permission, install, hook, oauth, plus named harness installers, .githooks/, the orch seat-guard and access_guards migrations; guard alone is no stem. Only hook is excluded under src/, web/ and server-admin-web/; harness knowledge markdown is documentation. Jev unavailable or cut input (80,000-character cap or gate alteration) gives one, or two with changed own security lines, labelled. Returns vendored paths left out and jevRisk (null when not scored). A Jev weakens_tests probability of 0.5 or more adds weakensTests and a focus line (plan and theme); it never changes the count. Multiple code domains return independent themes [{theme, paths, stats, count, reason, focus, vendored, jevRisk}]; total count is their sum. Create one reviewer set per theme, briefed on only its own paths (decision #12934); unmatched code is unrouted, documentation joins no theme. Read-only on the repository.

seat.description: Coder seat id; exclusive with repo/base/snapshot.

repo.description: Absolute Git checkout to inspect, when no seat is given.

base.description: Diff current checkout against this commit/ref.

snapshot.description: Diff HEAD against current checkout when no base is provided.

tools.name: seat_close
tools.description: Close a seat: a running turn is cancelled, a reviewer worktree removed; a coder branch and worktree stay. While provisioning, answers immediately with closePending: true and status provisioning; closure and cleanup wait for setup to finish. A seat whose setup a restart drain holds has made nothing yet and closes at once (status closed).

tools.name: seat_create
tools.description: Create a worker seat. coder: own worktree on branch orch/<seat> from `base` (kept after close for you to land); tester: own branch worktree, same landing as a coder, outside the coder cap and without coder rechecks; designer: own branch worktree like a coder that may only write src/**/*.tsx, src/**/*.css and web/apps/**, on this Mac or a host with the Bright Data key, reading images by default; copywriter: own branch worktree that may only write web/apps/** and src/locales/**, on this Mac or a host with the Bright Data key; motion: own branch worktree like a coder that may only write web/apps/landing/public/media/** and web/apps/landing/_drafts/motion/**, on this Mac only (the Higgsfield session and ffmpeg-full exist only here), reading images by default; legal: disposable detached worktree with reviewer rights (`base` or `snapshot`, author and coauthors step aside, nothing lands), on this Mac or a host with the Bright Data key; security: disposable detached worktree with reviewer rights, max effort where the route supports it (kimi, mimo: high); reviewer: disposable detached worktree at `base` or a `snapshot`, reviewing the ACCUMULATED diff once per task, at most 2 per task (same title), a recheck is a turn of one of them (a closed reviewer without a valid report does not count, nor one a recheck superseded, whose family stays out); bughunter: hunts reproduced defects in existing code at max effort (kimi: high), disposable worktree; scout/researcher: read the repo in place and answer ONE question; a scout reports facts only, never a design or a how-to (#17974). debater: read the repo in place, answer one question, then one rebuttal of the other side's done first turn (`seat_prompt` `rebut`); give the two debaters of a fork ONE title, and orch keeps them on different models. Leave `family` out: orch picks a family at or behind pace first, by need, then by pace headroom on the longest readable budget window; shorter windows throttle, equal-length model-scoped windows throttle only matching models, calibrated burn may veto, and unreadable usage ranks last. Paused families are excluded even from the emergency choice, and explicit requests for them are refused. Your own family (except for a coder seat or an eligible claude reviewer/plan critic), the author's and every coauthor's step aside. For a multi-slice task reviewed once, pass `author` and `coauthors` naming the other coder seats whose change is in the diff (reviewer or plan critic). The one reviewer exception is claude, which may review a named non-claude author only when every coauthor is also non-claude, even when claude is your family. Without `author`, or with a claude author or coauthor, claude never reviews, even when named explicitly. A claude plan critic may omit `author` and may share your family, but is excluded when any named author or coauthor is claude, even when named explicitly (#13875). Model and effort come from the role matrix. A family outside the role's matrix is refused. With `host`, Pi seats may run remotely: orch prepares a checkout on that host, refusing a SHA/tree mismatch; researcher, designer, copywriter and legal require the brightdata-web capability (BRIGHTDATA_API_KEY in the host environment or its prefixed secrets file); this Mac always offers it. Claude, motion, native harnesses and stand arms stay on this Mac. Local editing worktrees are provisioned like Paseo ones (npm ci, codegraph index, skills), so the seat is `provisioning` while setup runs; a prompt given meanwhile waits for it. Harness defaults to Pi for every family except claude, which runs native Claude Code (decision #11849: Pi's anthropic route bills the Max OAuth as extra usage); pass native for any family's own CLI, pi to opt claude into Pi explicitly. The answer carries `picked` (why this family), the seat's effective `instruments`, and, when load is high, a `warning`. A plan critic is `role: 'critic'`. The `critic` flag is an alias kept for one release: `role: 'scout'` with `critic: true` makes the same seat. Pass `images: true` when the seat must read images: each family whose model for this seat has no image input leaves the field before the pick, and neither the emergency choice nor the coder cap brings that family back. A role whose default skill requires image input is treated as `images: true` even when the flag is omitted. The effective value is stored on the seat; a `request_id` retry with a different value is refused. A debater round table (operator #19423) passes `options` (2-4 strings): every open debater of the same title must carry the identical list, and orch stores the lead-chat handle your `session` holds so the table's one tally post reaches you. Omit `options` for the classic two-side fork, which behaves exactly as before. A coder created with `files` also gets a non-blocking `warning` when every file is a test, fixture or capture (a tester seat fits) or any file is under src/locales/ (a copywriter seat fits). role 'auto' (pass `brief` and non-empty `files`): orch picks the role itself — tester when every file is a test, fixture or capture, or when Jev reads a tests-only brief or a reported defect (a defect brief gains the Test 0 line: the tester writes the red test first, then a coder fixes it), else coder — creates exactly that one seat and queues the brief as its first turn. The answer adds `turn`, `wait` and `picked` {role, rule, jev: {wide, defect, tests_only, look, logic}, next}. Jev unavailable or a brief its gate would cut refuses with no seat created; a wide reading above 0.85 refuses like the coder scope gate and `wide_brief` bypasses it. After an orch restart your MCP client must reconnect before role 'auto' reaches its cached copy of this schema.

brief.description: role 'auto' only: the brief orch reads to pick tester or coder; it is queued as the seat's first turn and the seat_prompt 300-word rule applies.

wide_brief.description: role 'auto' only: why the work cannot be split when Jev reads the brief wider than 0.85; the same bypass as seat_prompt. At most 300 characters after trimming.

session.description: Your hook session id, the same one the chat tools take. The own-family step-aside then covers only your family, and orch stores it on the seat so its own recheck reviewer steps aside from your family too (decision #17805 D2). Without it, or when it does not resolve, every lead active in the last 10 minutes steps aside and `picked` says so.

family.description: Omit to pick a family at or behind pace first, by need, then by pace headroom, among unpaused families; a paused explicit family is refused.

author.description: reviewer/plan critic: the primary coder seat whose change this reviews; its family never reviews it. Claude reviewers require a named non-claude author and only non-claude coauthors. Claude plan critics may omit author, but every named author/coauthor must be non-claude; both may share a claude lead family.

coauthors.description: reviewer/plan critic: for a multi-slice task reviewed once, the other existing coder seats whose change is in the diff. Requires author; each family is excluded, even when family is named explicitly.

title.description: What the seat is for, one line.

repo.description: Absolute path of your checkout; the seat works in this repository.

base.description: Commit or ref for a coder/bughunter worktree (default HEAD of `repo`); a reviewer needs it or `snapshot`.

snapshot.description: coder/reviewer: check out your working tree as it is now, uncommitted and untracked files included, as one commit on top of HEAD; the change is `git diff HEAD^` in the seat. Use it to review work you have not committed. Exclusive with base.

host.description: Named remote host for a Pi seat; researcher, designer, copywriter and legal require brightdata-web (the host holds BRIGHTDATA_API_KEY). Claude, motion, native harness and standArm cannot use a remote host.

needs.description: Platform need: omitted defaults to any (decision #12591), probing this Mac and registered hosts and choosing the highest free capacity (free cores and free memory) for Pi seats of every role when hosts exist; with no registered hosts it stays on this Mac without probing, and if all probes fail it falls back to this Mac. mac pins this Mac without probing; win requires a win32 host. Claude, motion, native harness and standArm seats stay on this Mac when needs is omitted; explicit non-mac needs with native harness, standArm or motion are refused. Researcher, designer, copywriter and legal may use hosts offering brightdata-web (BRIGHTDATA_API_KEY); this Mac always offers it. No eligible target refuses creation. Explicit host chooses the machine instead of default placement. The seat row carries placement {needs, target, reason}.

needs_reason.description: Required with needs mac unless a file is this Mac's desktop runtime or the seat is claude, native or a stand arm (task 3288): what on this Mac the seat must touch (the Tauri runtime, state under ~/.local/state, a loopback service, Mac-only credentials, uncommitted files read in place). Stored in the placement reason. Refused without needs mac.

files.description: Repo-relative paths the task is about, used to apply configured placement rules. Omit if not known at creation.

request_id.description: Idempotency key: a retry of a create whose answer was lost (client timeout) passes the same request_id and gets the existing seat back instead of a duplicate.

standArm.description: A/B stand only: explicit isolated Pi profile. Omit for a stock seat; never pass a config path.

critic.description: `role: 'critic'` is a plan critic; this flag is an alias kept for one release (`role: 'scout'` with `critic: true` makes the same seat) (#13286, #13875) — the scout lifecycle (one question, no worktree) on the whole reviewer matrix: its family pool, model and high effort. The plan author's seat may be named in `author`; its family and every coauthor's never take the seat. Your own family steps aside even when named explicitly, except claude may take the seat when no named author or coauthor is claude. `model`, `effort`, an explicit native harness and a family outside the reviewer matrix are refused; omitted harness runs claude natively with the matrix model.

images.description: True when this seat must read images. Each family whose model for this seat has no image input leaves the field before the pick, including the emergency choice and the coder cap. Omitted is false, except a role whose default skill requires image input, which is true either way. Stored on the seat; a request_id retry with a different value is refused.

options.description: debater round table (operator #19423): the 2-4 option strings every member votes on; every open debater of the same title must carry the identical list. Omit for the classic two-side fork.

instruments.description: Per-seat instrument override (task 1452): false turns that instrument off for this seat alone; omitted leaves every instrument on. RTK is never an arm.

codegraph.description: The codegraph MCP tool and CLI.

memory.description: The memoryctl MCP tool and CLI.

tools.name: seat_land
tools.description: Apply a coder or tester seat's accumulated committed, staged, unstaged and untracked changes since its base to the lead checkout (or into). Refuses dirty overlapping paths. A role write scope refuses patch paths outside it and lists them; override_reason lands those paths and stores the reason on the seat. Leaves conflicts in the lead checkout for resolution or rollback; never commits.

into.description: Optional absolute path to another checkout of the same repository; default the seat's original repo.

override_reason.description: Land patch paths outside the seat role write scope and store this reason on the seat. Omitted: those paths are refused and listed.

tools.name: seat_prompt
tools.description: Give a seat its task; returns with the queued turn id and its own wait command. A first coder, tester or bughunter brief with no files (in `files` or at seat_create) is refused: pass the repo-relative files of the area (decision #17906). A coder first brief is Jev-scored for scope bloat: only above 0.85 it is refused; pass wide_brief with why it cannot be split to bypass; the trimmed reason is stored on the seat. Jev unavailable or a cut brief passes labelled in the turn digest. After a coder correction turn finishes, its digest lists the automatic rechecks of reproduced reviewer blocker and major findings: kind `same` is a turn of that reviewer when every path the correction changes is named in those findings; kind `new` is a new reviewer of another family over the whole diff, replacing it, when the correction changes any other path (decision #12435); set recheck:false on that prompt to opt out. A follow-up to a busy seat queues FIFO behind its running turn (at most 5 queued); you can wait on either turn independently. Coder answers include overlap: [{seat, files, more}] and overlapUnchecked: [seat] for worktree observations that failed; both warn only. `prompt` is the brief: English, at most 300 words (task, owned files, evidence, acceptance; link larger artifacts). A debater's second turn requires `rebut`: the turn id of another debater's done first turn with a parsed report; that report's claims, evidence and forLead are appended verbatim to the stored brief, outside the 300-word count. `rebut` on any other role or on a first turn is refused, and so is one between two seats that run the same model: the two debaters of a fork share ONE title and orch keeps them apart. orch wraps a seat's first brief in its role context (knowledge pages and lessons for `files`, code-intel rules, routed skills) and every turn ends in the role's JSON report contract (one fenced block, aimed under 5500 characters with each claim under 300; size is never refused); a reply off the schema gets up to two repair turns naming every fault, and the digest carries only the parsed `report`. Then wait WITHOUT polling: in Claude Code run the returned `wait` command as a background Bash task (you are notified with the digest); elsewhere call seat_wait. A first coder brief also carries a non-blocking `warning` when a specialist seat fits: tester (every file a test, fixture or capture, or Jev reads a tests-only brief), designer (Jev reads a surface-look change over a UI file), copywriter (a src/locales/ file), and a reported defect without a reproducing test (a tester writes the red test first).

files.description: Repo-relative files the task is about; they select knowledge pages and lessons.

long_brief.description: Only for a brief over 300 words: why it cannot be shorter.

wide_brief.description: Coder first brief only: why the work cannot be split into sequential seats (max 300 characters after trimming); bypasses the Jev scope gate.

token_cap.description: Stand Pi seats only: abort after this many cumulative input+output+cacheRead tokens; a single response may overshoot.

recheck.description: Coder correction only: false suppresses automatic rechecks of reproduced reviewer blocker and major findings.

rebut.description: Debater second turn only: the turn id of another debater's done first turn, or `table` for a round-table member (created with `options`) to see every other member's anonymized round-1 report. Required on that turn; refused on any other role or on a first turn.

tools.name: seat_report
tools.description: The raw final message of a turn. Read it ONLY when the JSON report in the digest is missing or you could not understand it: the report is the delivery.

tools.name: seat_wait
tools.description: Wait up to `seconds` (max 50) for a turn; returns a compact text digest with flags, findings, checks and notes. Use `json: true` for the full digest including grade, watch and worktree. A null report names seat_report for raw text. No flags: accept the report as it stands; a flag names what to check. Prefer the background `wait` command in Claude Code.

json.description: Return the full JSON digest instead of text.

tools.name: seats_list
tools.description: List seats known to orch. Open seats: every one, oldest first, full row. Omits closed seats unless `closed` is true or `status` is `closed`; closed seats come newest first, `limit` per page (default 50), in a compact row (id, role, family, title, status, last turn id and status, ended, failure) with `closedPage` naming the omitted count and the next `offset`. Optional exact status filter. `seat` returns that one seat in full whatever its status.

seat.description: Exactly this seat id, in the full row whatever its status, no paging; [] when unknown. Not combined with the other arguments.

status.description: Only seats with this status. The value closed returns closed seats even when the closed flag is omitted.

closed.description: Include closed seats. Default false. An exact `status` still applies.

limit.description: Closed seats per page, newest first. Default 50. Open seats are never limited.

offset.description: Closed seats to skip, newest first: pass the previous answer's closedPage.nextOffset. Default 0.
